title: Space Colonization
description: Command your space fleet in a tactical chess-style battle for galactic dominance. Deploy your Space Station, Flagship, Battlecruisers, Scout Ships, Fighter Squadrons, and Drones across an 8x8 star grid. Capture enemy vessels, seize strategic planets and asteroid belts, and build your fleet's power rating to 10 million to claim victory among the stars.
learning_objectives: Develop strategic spatial reasoning by controlling key sectors of the galactic grid
Practice resource management by balancing fleet movements with territory acquisition
Learn positional advantage concepts through fleet formation and sector control
Build risk assessment skills by evaluating when to engage or retreat from combat
Understand the value of sacrifice and trade-offs in achieving long-term strategic goals
Strengthen multi-step planning by coordinating multiple fleet units toward victory conditions
how_to_play: Each turn you receive 2 Action Points (AP). Moving a ship costs 1 AP, and using a special ability costs AP as listed on the ability.
Ships move like chess pieces: Station=King, Flagship=Queen, Cruiser=Rook, Scout Ship=Bishop, Fighter=Knight, Drone=Pawn.
Engage enemy ships by moving onto their square to deal damage. Drones promote to Flagship when reaching the far edge of the grid.
Control resource sectors by positioning your ships on them. Each sector generates power income every turn.
Win by destroying the enemy Space Station, controlling 3 or more resource sectors, or reaching 10 million power rating.
Use special abilities wisely: each ship has two unique abilities that can turn the tide of battle at critical moments.
objectives: Destroy the rival Space Station to achieve an instant tactical victory
Control 3 or more resource sectors for a territorial dominance victory
Build your fleet power rating to 10 million through strategic income generation

storybook_pages.title: The Galactic Frontier
storybook_pages.text: Two rival space fleets converge on an uncharted sector of the galaxy. Planets rich in resources, asteroid belts full of rare minerals, and mysterious wormholes dot the star grid. Your mission: deploy your fleet, seize control of strategic sectors, and outmaneuver the enemy commander before they do the same to you.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: two massive space fleets facing each other across a glowing 8x8 star grid with planets and asteroid belts scattered across it, dramatic nebula background, sci-fi digital art, cinematic lighting

storybook_pages.title: Your Fleet
storybook_pages.text:
Space Station (King) - Your command center, lose it and the war is over.
Flagship (Queen) - Your most powerful vessel, capable of any maneuver.
Battlecruiser (Rook) - Straight-line firepower that dominates corridors.
Scout Ship (Bishop) - Diagonal reconnaissance and flanking specialist.
Fighter Squadron (Knight) - Unpredictable L-shaped strike craft.
Drone (Pawn) - Expendable units that can be promoted to Flagship!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: lineup of six different sci-fi spacecraft ranging from a massive space station to tiny drones, each with distinct silhouettes, holographic display style, blueprint aesthetic with glowing lines

storybook_pages.title: The Sectors of Power
storybook_pages.text: The star grid contains 6 strategic resource sectors: Planet Alpha provides habitable territory, the Asteroid Belt yields rare minerals, a Wormhole offers tactical shortcuts, a Nebula hides sensor signatures, the Space Dock repairs damaged ships, and the Fuel Depot extends your operational range. Control them to fuel your fleet's expansion!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: birds eye view of a glowing 8x8 space grid with six highlighted sectors showing a planet, asteroid belt, wormhole portal, colorful nebula, orbital space dock, and fuel station, sci-fi strategy game map art

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.
